figures.finding: A Rarotonga resident pays no tax on the first NZD 14,600, then 17% on the next 15,400 (to 30,000), 27% on the next 50,000 (to 80,000) and 30% above; a resident of the outer islands (Pa Enua) pays nothing on the first 60,000, then 27% to 80,000 and 30% above.

value.exemptionProRata: by days present when arriving or leaving in the year

figures.applies: The 2025 income year's returns, the latest issued (no 2026 return or rate change found); the Pa Enua return form for 2025 shows the outer-island scale.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; an employee's return is due 1 March, a business's (including a sole trader's) 1 May, and any tax owing is paid by 1 November after the year.

sources.said: The standard tax year is 1st January - 31 December
due date for filing your income tax return is 1st March following the year you are filing.
tax is the 1st of November following the tax year.

figures.finding: Every employer contributes 5% of gross salary to the Cook Islands National Superannuation Fund and deducts 5% from the employee, monthly; no other payroll social contribution was found.
figures.applies: Employees under the Cook Islands National Superannuation Act 2000; foreign workers may withdraw on permanent departure.

sources.said: The standard contribution rate is 10% of gross salary, split between employer (5%) and employee (5%).
Contributions are compulsory under the CINSF Act 2000

figures.finding: The employer deducts PAYE from wages by the PAYE schedule (from 1 January 2021 on Rarotonga; a separate schedule for the Pa Enua from 1 July 2023), with no tax on weekly income below NZD 281, and pays it by the 20th of the following month.
figures.applies: Employees; a sole trader pays on assessment.

sources.said: No tax on weekly incomes below......... $281 PAYE SCHEDULE FROM 1 JANUARY 2021
any wages paid to employees and PAYE tax deducted from their wages must be declared in the RM205 form and paid every 20th of the month.

figures.finding: Royalties paid to a non-resident bear 15% non-resident withholding tax; no withholding specific to a non-resident performer's fee was found.
figures.applies: Non-residents; withholding income is interest, dividends, natural resource amounts or royalties.

sources.said: Non-resident Withholding Royalty (15%)
Withholding income is interest, dividends, natural resource amounts or royalties derived in the Cook Islands but paid to a person who is not a resident.

figures.finding: VAT is 15%; a business must register once turnover passes NZD 40,000 over 12 months (voluntary registration needs over 20,000).
figures.applies: Taxable activities in the Cook Islands.

sources.said: was over $40,000 for the last 12 months,
charge VAT at 15% on all your sales, except those ex- empt from VAT

figures.finding: The Income Tax Act gives authors no special treatment: royalties and like payments for the use of any property are ordinary assessable income at the resident scale, and royalties paid to a non-resident bear the 15% non-resident withholding tax.
figures.applies: Income Tax Act 1997 s 46(1)(e) and Part IX; MFEM RM100 return.
